subject: Evaluation playbook, decision owners, and contract ticketing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aurelia.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + proposed evaluation playbook and next steps

Hi Tom — great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking us through Aurelia's priorities and the performance bar you need for transcript summarization at peak load. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Decision criteria you called out: latency under 150ms median for 512 tokens, consistent hallucination rate <1%, and ability to run within your VPC for PII data.
- Economic buyer: you mentioned Emma (legal), and procurement intake will own contracts.
- Security owners: Emma and your InfoSec lead (you’ll share contact).

Proposed evaluation playbook (attached): redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf — short PoC (3 weeks):
1) Week 1: PoC config + baseline latency tests (hosted dedicated sim).
2) Week 2: Data residency & minimal private connector test (one API route).
3) Week 3: Accuracy/regression checks using your internal prompt set; handoff to procurement for contract/terms.

Immediate asks: can you confirm the InfoSec contact and the procurement intake email? Also, I can kick off an NDA if that helps unblock the security review — do you prefer we start with our standard NDA or your template?

Attaching the playbook and a short RFI template to speed review. Happy to adjust cadence if you have a different procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aurelia.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed evaluation playbook and next steps

Thanks Soojin — nice summary. A couple quick clarifications:
- InfoSec lead is Emma Cho (cc’d here) — she’ll own the security questionnaire.
- Procurement email is procurement@aurelia.ai (I’ve looped the team on separate threads but including here for visibility).
- For NDA, we prefer to use our vendor NDA template first, but we’re open to Redwood’s if it speeds things up.

I’ve shared the playbook with Emma and procurement. Can you also include an estimated cost range for the PoC (hosted + dedicated burst) so procurement has numbers for their intake form?

Tom
Tom Reynolds | Head of Product | Aurelia Labs

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Aurelia PoC — owners, pricing, and legal sequencing (for handoff)

Team — quick internal note after the demo with Aurelia. External thread: Tom Reynolds / Emma Cho / procurement@aurelia.ai. Key asks: PoC cost estimate for procurement, security questionnaire, and NDA template preference (they prefer their NDA but flexible).

Proposed internal owners/timeframes:
- AE (me): program lead, customer contact, timeline owner.
- SE (Logan): PoC configuration + baseline tests, start Mon Feb 16.
- CS/Commercial ops (Marissa): pricing worksheet and procurement intake support; produce PoC estimate by EOD Thu Feb 12.
- Deal economics (Ben): draft commercial guardrails (trial discounts, usage caps) and pricing ranges.

Legal/contract sequencing recommendation (based on standard Redwood playbook):
1) NDA (can accept Aurelia NDA) — target turnaround 3 business days.
2) Security review + RFI answers (Emma) — concurrent with NDA review.
3) MSA redline session only after PoC confirms fit — reduces negotiation surface.

Attachments for Handoff: redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf, Aurelia-RFI-security-answers.xlsx (seed answers)

Can Marissa confirm she has capacity to own the procurement intake? Ben — I’ll need a quick guidance note on acceptable concession ranges.

Thanks — Soojin

(Internal-only: do not forward attachments externally until procurement gives go-ahead)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Aurelia PoC — owners, pricing, and legal sequencing (for handoff)

On it — I’ll draft the procurement estimate and include two options: small PoC (burst hosted + 1 dedicated node for load) and conservative PoC (dedicated pool + higher call volume). Targeting EOD Thu 2/12.

Ben — do you have a % discount range we can offer for a 3-week PoC to land the trial (thinking 40-60% list depending on committed usage)? If we can add a token cap and a one-time evaluation credit as safety, that will help procurement sign off.

Logan — can you capture the baseline test checklist (latency profile, sample prompt set) and share by Friday?

Marissa
Senior Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aurelia.ai>, Emma Cho <emma.cho@aurelia.ai>, procurement@aurelia.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed evaluation playbook and next steps — PoC cost + contract flow

Hi Tom / Emma / procurement team — thanks for the quick replies and for looping Emma. Attaching a short cost estimate we prepared (two PoC options) and an RFI seed file to speed the security review.

High level estimate (summary, details attached):
- Option A (fast path) — 3-week lightweight PoC using hosted + one dedicated node: est. $12k - $18k (includes engineering support and one training session).
- Option B (comprehensive) — 3-week dedicated pool + extended load testing: est. $28k - $36k.

Contract flow recommendation:
1) NDA (prefer using Aurelia NDA) — once signed, we’ll share full RFI answers and deeper architecture notes.
2) Security review (Emma) — we’ll provide the RFI and set up a 60-min call with our security engineer.
3) Procurement intake — Marissa will provide the final estimate and a one-page SOW.

Next steps for procurement: please share any intake form, PO format, and target review SLA (typical procurement turnaround at Aurelia?). If you prefer, I can drop a short DocuSign NDA (Aurelia NDA attached as a PDF if you send it) to accelerate.

Thanks,
Soojin
(Attachments: redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf, Aurelia-RFI-security-answers.xlsx)
From: procurement@aurelia.ai
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aurelia.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed evaluation playbook and next steps — PoC cost + contract flow

Hi Soojin — thanks for the estimate and materials. A few housekeeping items from procurement: 
1) Please fill out our vendor intake form (link below) with the estimated PoC cost and any insurance certs.
2) We prefer to start with our NDA template (attached). Please review and return redline within 3 business days.
3) Typical procurement SLA is 5-7 business days for NDA review, longer for MSA depending on redlines.

We’ve attached the vendor intake PDF and the Aurelia_NDA_v2.pdf. Once we have the signed NDA and the intake form, we’ll schedule the security intake call.

Procurement Team
Aurelia Labs
(Attachment: Aurelia_NDA_v2.pdf)
